LESSON: WRITING 9.4.1 PUNCTUATION (THE COMMA)

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade two
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.4: Writing 9.4.1 Punctuation (The comma)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 9.4.1 Punctuation (The comma), part of Strand 9 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade two General.

Key inquiry question: Why do you think we use a comma when writing?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 9.4.1 Punctuation (The comma) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: as they engage in group practice exercises to write using a comma.

• Digital literacy: is enhanced as the learner writes sentences with commas on digital devices.

Values:
Responsibility: as learners takes up roles during role play activities.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Citizenship (social cohesion): as learners work together to identify commas in lists and sentences.

Links to other Learning Areas:
Use of comma is emphasized in Kiswahili and Indigenous Language Activities.

Suggested Learning Resources:

Sample handwritings on wall charts/digital devices, assistive technology such as universal cuffs/wrist braces/arm braces, weighted pencil/pen

grips, page-turners, adapted digital devices with filter keys/key guards/larger mouse/head control input devices such as head wand
